use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

claims.content: If a C2 JU receives a Correlation message in which the Track Number Applicability Indicator is set to value 0 (indicating the track is not accepted), the C2 JU shall terminate the correlation process. The receiving C2 JU shall then initiate the de-correlation process as described in paragraph 4.4.3.1.

If an operator rejects a proposed correlation (e.g., via a manual rejection action or by setting the Identity Difference Indicator to value 1 in response to a J7.0 message), the system shall abort the automatic correlation process for those specific tracks. The tracks will continue to be reported separately.

If a C2 JU attempts to correlate a track with itself (a 'self-correlation'), the system shall detect this condition and reject the correlation attempt, maintaining the original track without modification.

If a C2 JU receives a J12.0 message containing invalid data (e.g., incorrect format, out-of-range values) that prevents processing, the C2 JU shall discard the message and may generate an error report or alert for the operator, but shall not update any track data based on the invalid message.

If a communication failure occurs during the transmission of a surveillance track message (e.g., J7.0, J12.0), and the message is not acknowledged by the receiver, the sending system's communication protocol (not specified in this document) will handle the retransmission or failure notification. The use case for publishing the track is considered incomplete until successful transmission is confirmed.

The C2 JU has transmitted a J7.0 message containing the complete surveillance track data (including Track Number Applicability Indicator set to value 1) to the designated recipient(s) via the appropriate interface.
The receiving system(s) have acknowledged receipt of the J7.0 message (implied by successful completion of the 'publish' action within the scope of this use case).

If correlation was performed as part of publishing (e.g., merging local and remote tracks), the correlated track data is consistent across participating systems, with the Track Number Applicability Indicator correctly set to reflect acceptance (value 1) or rejection (value 0) by each participant.

Any associated identity information (J12.0 messages) required for the published track(s) has been transmitted and synchronized with the track data, ensuring receivers can properly associate identity with the track.
The published track(s) are now available for display, further processing, or dissemination by the receiving system(s) according to their own operational rules and filter settings.
